01 — THE PROBLEM

A $16,000 failure hiding in plain sight

The vehicle recovery industry processes 10.5 million repo assignments annually — and fails on 70% of them. Each unrecovered vehicle costs a lender approximately $16,000. The problem wasn't the repossessors. It was the workflow.

Industry reality
Skip tracers were flying blind

Recovery agents relied on LPR cameras and skip-tracing — reactive, slow, expensive methods with no way to predict where a vehicle would be at a specific time of day.

Motorq's opportunity
OEM telematics = unfair advantage

Motorq's direct OEM data pipeline gave access to real-time vehicle location, trip history, and behavioral data that no competitor could touch. The question: could we turn that into a workflow that actually recovered vehicles?

This is what I watched a recovery manager at BridgeCrest — a DriveTime subsidiary managing $149M in revenue — do live in our first discovery session with my PM and Product VP. That single observation became the entire design foundation.

02 — COMPETITIVE BENCHMARKING

What already existed — and why it wasn't enough

Before designing, I studied Recovr — the closest product in market — alongside RDN, the 90% market-share incumbent. Understanding where each fell short shaped exactly what we built differently.

CapabilityRecovrRDN (incumbent)Manual workflowVehicle Recovery Console
Real-time location✓ Hardware GPS tracker required✗ Relies on skip tracers~ Via Motorq portal manually✓ OEM telematics, zero hardware
AI location prediction✗ No prediction✗ None✗ Human inference from Excel✓ Daytime + overnight, 77% accuracy
Works on existing fleet✗ Device install per vehicle✓ Assignment-based✓✓ Any OEM-connected vehicle
Unified workflow~ Mobile app, dealer-only~ Assignment mgmt only✗ 5 separate apps✓ Triage → recommendation → handoff in one console
Confidence scoring✗✗✗✓ High / Medium / Low on every recommendation
Live tracking (theft)✓ Hardware + law enforcement link✗✗✓ 10–15s latency via OEM, no hardware
Fleet triage view✗✗✗✓ Vehicle Priority View — rank by recovery confidence
💡
What benchmarking actually revealed

When I first looked at Recovr, I expected to find something close to what we were building — and figure out how to differentiate. What I found instead was that Recovr had solved a completely different problem. Their product assumes the vehicle has already been stolen and a hardware tracker is already installed. Ours assumes neither. They're reactive; we're predictive. The moment I understood that, the competitive question simplified entirely: we weren't competing with Recovr. We were building something that didn't exist yet — a workflow tool for lenders that turns telematics data into recovery decisions before an agent ever leaves the office. No one had built that. That's when I felt confident we were working on the right thing.

03 — THE USER

Sitting next to the person who does this every day

My PM, Product VP, and I got direct access to two recovery managers at BridgeCrest. We watched them do the job live — not just describe it. That session changed everything about how we scoped the product.

PRIMARY USER
Recovery / Repossession Manager

Manages a portfolio of vehicles flagged for recovery. On any Monday morning they may have 40 vehicles to prioritise — only a handful have enough trip data for the AI to generate confident recommendations. Their job is triage: which vehicles can we realistically recover in the next 24 hours?

Core frustration"I'm jumping between five tools for every single vehicle. By the time I figure out where it might be, I've spent two hours on one VIN."
SECONDARY USER
FMC Field Agent / Skip Tracer

On the ground, often coordinating with police in real time. Needs precise, confident location recommendations — not raw data. When tracking a stolen vehicle, seconds matter. They previously relied on RDN's recommendations; they now ask for Motorq's AI recommendations instead.

Core needFast, trustworthy location data with a best recovery window. Live tracking available when the vehicle is actively moving.
"When they saw everything in one place, the reaction was immediate — this is going to save so much time. And when they saw the AI recommendations, they asked: when can we start using this?"
— Recovery Manager, BridgeCrest · First product review session

That first session wasn't the end of research — it was the beginning. We ran a standing Wednesday sync with BridgeCrest's recovery managers through Phase 1 and Phase 2, reviewing how the product performed in real use each week. Those calls are where the hardest feedback came: the trust challenge that led to the heatmap, the request for secondary recommendations, and eventually the proposal for the Vehicle Priority View. The product you see today is the output of that ongoing dialogue — not a single discovery session translated directly into screens.
